div.head: III Em 4
div.ab: Et dictum est de seruis: si qui furentur simul, ut senior ex eis capiatur et occidatur uel suspendatur, et aliorum singuli uerberentur ter et excorientur[?], et truncetur minimus digitus in signum.
Et dictum est de servis: si qui furentur, senior ex eis capiatur et occidatur vel suspendatur, et aliorum singuli verberentur ter et extoppentur, et truncetur minimus digitus in signum.

And we have declared with regard to slaves that, if a number of them commit theft, their leader shall be captured and slain, or hanged, and each of the others shall be scourged three times and have his scalp removed and his little finger mutilated as a token of his guilt.
div.note: Latin only; no German translation in Liebermann. ‘excorientur’ is Liebermann's emendation (T extopentur; MHk -topp-; Br -torp-), after ‘hættie’ in II Cn 30.5.
